title: Shantanu's promise
hook: a woman rises from the river and sits on a praying king's right thigh; years later his son gives her his word
tomorrow: what will Shantanu's promise cost him?

segments.voice: Yesterday: Mahabhisha, a stare in Brahma's court, and gods who wanted release. Karma carries into the next birth.

A king is sitting by the river, deep in prayer. His name is Pratipa. Out of the water rises a woman of great beauty, and she sits down on his right thigh. Pratipa doesn't send her away, and he doesn't take her as a lover. Instead he tells her: the right thigh is for children and daughters-in-law. The left is for a wife. You sat on the right, so you'll be my son's wife.
screen: `A WOMAN RISES FROM THE RIVER.` → `SHE SITS ON THE RIGHT THIGH.` → `YOU'LL BE MY SON'S WIFE.`

segments.voice: The woman is Ganga, and she agrees: she'll marry Pratipa's son, on one condition, that whatever she does, he won't question it. A son is born: Shantanu, who is Mahabhisha come down from heaven. When Shantanu is grown, Pratipa hands him the kingdom, and a message with it. A lovely woman may come to you. If she does, take her as your wife. Don't ask who she is, and don't question what she does. One day, walking along the bank of the Ganga, Shantanu sees a woman by the water, and he's struck. He asks her to be his wife. She answers with terms. Whatever I do, good or bad, you must never stop me or speak harshly to me. The moment you do, I'll leave. He agrees. Now notice what we know that he doesn't: she's Ganga, and she's promised the Vasus. He knows only that he's in love, and that he's given his word. In this epic, a given word is never small talk. Keeping it is dharma, and the Mahabharata tests that again and again; one vow coming soon will shape the whole Kuru line. Hindus still make their biggest promises out loud and witnessed. At a wedding, the couple circles the sacred fire and takes seven steps together, the saptapadi, with Agni, the fire, as witness. Shantanu's vow had no fire and no family, only a riverbank and a man in love, and it will hold his tongue for years. They marry, and the text says they're happy together. And their first child is on the way.
screen: `SHANTANU: MAHABHISHA REBORN.` · `A FATHER'S MESSAGE: DON'T ASK.` · `HER TERMS: NEVER STOP ME.` · `A WORD IS NEVER SMALL TALK.` · then, large: `KEEPING YOUR WORD IS DHARMA.`

segments.voice: Write down, by hand, one promise you're carrying right now: to a person, a team, yourself. If you can, light a candle or a small lamp beside it, the way a Hindu wedding keeps the fire as witness. Read the promise once, out loud. Then ask, gently: do I still know what this promise asks of me?
Pratipa. The king who, when Ganga sat on his right thigh, told her she'd be his son's wife, and whose warning led Shantanu to vow never to question her.
One line for today: keeping your word is dharma. Tomorrow: what will Shantanu's promise cost him? Day seven hundred five, done.
